items.title: Player interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2012
items.q: But I think when I met my high school band director, Larry Pinell was made I was kind of like going out playing gigs, like when I did something with his band.

ctx.x: Can you remember the first time you made money playing a gig, and how much was it?

I think the first time I actually made money, I think it probably had to be about ninth grade I think. I had already been doing some classical performances, like orchestras and stuff, and my junior high school orchestra teacher had even gotten some of her students who excelled to perform, to do some performances, like pops concerts with the professional symphonies. We’d play with the Marshall Texas Symphony and the Shreveport Symphony early on. But I wasn’t making any money but I was there playing with the other…
That’s 66 more dollars than I made on my first gig.
